gen-fs-oswald-fs-plein: Oswald stands tall and tightly knit, its rows of text packed into a confident, strong block of display type. Plein follows in sans-serif, with a clear channel leading into each round letter.
gen-almendra-display-gf-noto-sans-avesta: Ornate and bookish, with a tall x-height and letters that never pinch shut, Almendra Display sets a literary tone right away. It does the flourish; Noto Sans Avestan handles the plain, modern sans work.
gen-fs-oswald-fs-amulya: Amulya reads as contemporary sans-serif, its curves leaving generous gaps that keep every word easy to take in. Oswald brings the confident, tightly knit strength up top, and Amulya simply does the quiet reading below.
gen-almendra-display-gf-noto-sans-baline: Almendra Display has an ornate, literary air, with a pronounced x-height and letters that never seem to pinch shut. Noto Sans Balinese brings breathing room inside every curve.
gen-almendra-display-gf-noto-sans-bamum: Ornate letters lead here, never pinching shut. Noto Sans Bamum follows with modern, clean sans shapes whose big open counters give Almendra Display's literary flourish somewhere quiet to rest.
gen-audiowide-fs-bespoke-sans: Futuristic is the first word that comes to mind, with Audiowide's tile-like glyphs set apart by wide grout lines. Bespoke Sans is the sharper, more refined partner, with generous space between curve ends and the stem.
gen-audiowide-gf-abeezee: ABeeZee reads as approachable sans, with terminals that finish well clear of the stem and a mean line set high. And Audiowide supplies the futuristic, tech-flavored punch, its tile-like glyphs sitting on top of that friendly texture.
gen-audiowide-gf-aldrich: Audiowide is all futuristic tech, its strokes showing no thick-thin shift and its glyphs laid out like tiles with wide grout lines. Aldrich is the plain sans partner, with an x-height close to the cap height and round letters that look cupped, not clenched.
gen-audiowide-gf-alexandria: Strokes pulled like solder through a nozzle give Audiowide its futuristic stamp, with tall lowercase against its capitals. And Alexandria, a clean plain sans, handles the text with wide open terminals and short stems above and below.
gen-audiowide-gf-amiko: Audiowide shows no shift in weight along any curve, like neon glass tubing. Amiko, in sans-serif, brings crayon-mark-tall lowercase strokes and outward-pointing terminals, so a bit more size suggests itself for the text.
